title: Export Dispatcher with provenance ledgers and tenant calendar
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Goal: Build an Export Dispatcher that produces tenant-scoped compliance bundles (PDF/CSV) and a cryptographically verifiable provenance ledger, schedules recurring deliveries on a tenant calendar, and respects data residency and retention configurations.

Background: Customers in regulated industries need time-bound, auditable delivery of compliance artifacts: redacted transcripts, API call logs, model inference metadata, and retention proofs. Existing export jobs are ad-hoc and lack per-tenant residency enforcement or signed provenance for downstream auditors. This work ties together export formatting, residency-aware routing, retention filtering, and delivery scheduling into a first-class Console feature.

Key capabilities:
- Tenant calendar: allow per-tenant delivery cadence (daily, weekly, monthly, cron) with timezone and business-hour windows.
- Export payloads: multi-format bundles (PDF briefing + CSV raw rows) plus a manifest.json and cryptographic provenance ledger (hash chain + KMS-signed statement).
- Residency & retention enforcement: exports assembled only from data that matches tenant residency and retention policies; retained fields redacted per tenant rules.
- Dispatch options: S3 signed URL delivery, partner SFTP with host key fingerprinting, and secure webhook push with retry/backoff.
- Observability: per-dispatch dashboard showing size, time-to-generate, token counts, latency percentiles, and delivery status; alert on failed dispatches or residency violations.

Non-goals for this ticket: ad-hoc manual on-demand exports via API (will be follow-up), multi-tenant combined bundles (each dispatch is tenant-scoped), heavy-weight transformation engine for arbitrary formats (we'll support PDF/CSV + manifest initially).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Product UI: tenant calendar UI in Console where customers can configure cadence, timezone, delivery method, and retention snapshot date.
2) Backend: dispatcher service that creates ZIP bundles containing: PDF summary, CSV rows, manifest.json, and provenance.txt signed by tenant-specific KMS key.
3) Residency enforcement: dispatcher refuses to include records outside the tenant's configured residency regions; documented error path surfaced in UI and API.
4) Delivery: supports at least S3 signed URL and webhook delivery with retry policy; SFTP is beta behind feature flag.
5) Observability: new Console dashboard card per-tenant showing last 90 days of dispatches and a link to a delivery log; telemetry emits metrics for SLA reporting.
6) Security: export artifacts encrypted at rest per-customer KMS and provenance signatures validated in CI.

Release plan: staged rollout in console-2026.04; beta for selected enterprise tenants, monitor dispatch success rate > 99% and generation latency < 2 minutes for bundles under 100k rows before wider release.

Open questions and trade-offs:
- PDF generation engine: fastserver-side rendering (favors low-latency) vs asynchronous batch rendering for very large exports (favors throughput). Decided to do hybrid: synchronous up to 25k rows, background job beyond that.
- Manifest format: JSON manifest with a per-file SHA256 and a top-level merkle root vs simple hash chain. Chose hash chain with per-file SHA256 and a signed ledger to reduce parser complexity for auditors.
- Delivery guarantees: at-least-once S3 delivery vs exactly-once semantics. We'll provide idempotency keys and at-least-once semantics with dedupe support in downstream systems.

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Export+Dispatcher+Spec
- Design mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1X_export_dispatcher_ui
- Preliminary API shapes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-specs/pull/312

Next steps: finalize KMS integration with Security, implement ENG work items (ENG-2982: dispatcher core; ENG-3101: residency filter; ENG-3187: provenance signer), and schedule stakeholder review with Legal for auditability language.
